verdict: Oracle's revenue jumped 22% to $17.2B as cloud revenue surged 44% and its order backlog hit $553B — but $1.2B of interest on the debt funding the AI build-out held net income to $3.7B.

segments.name: Cloud
segments.note: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) revenue of $4.9B grew 84%, and cloud applications (SaaS) brought in $4.0B, up 13% — now 52% of all revenue.

segments.name: Software
segments.note: Traditional software licenses and support — still growing slightly as customers migrate to the cloud.

segments.name: Services
segments.note: Consulting and support services that help customers run Oracle products.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Building the cloud platform and the database software — up 7% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling to enterprises — actually down 3% YoY despite the growth push.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — finance, legal and the back office, flat YoY.

opex.name: Amortization of intangible assets
opex.note: Writing down the value of past acquisitions over time — a non-cash charge, down 25% YoY.

opex.name: Restructuring and other
opex.note: Restructuring charges of $153M plus $20M of acquisition-related costs — restructuring more than doubled YoY.

takeaways.title: The backlog exploded
takeaways.text: Remaining performance obligations hit $553B, up 325% in a year and up $29B in the quarter — mostly large AI contracts. Years of cloud revenue are already signed.

takeaways.title: Infrastructure is the engine
takeaways.text: Cloud infrastructure (OCI) revenue grew 84% to $4.9B; total cloud revenue was $8.9B, 52% of everything Oracle earns.

takeaways.title: Debt is the drag
takeaways.text: Interest expense rose 32% to $1.2B in the quarter as Oracle borrows to build data centers — the main reason net income ($3.7B) grew more slowly than operating income.

oneTimers: Restructuring charges of $153M — more than double the $63M of a year ago — sit inside operating expenses, alongside $20M of acquisition-related costs.
otherDetail: Interest expense of $1,180M on Oracle's growing debt pile, partly offset by $132M of non-operating income.
footerNote: Oracle reports its delivery costs as 'Cloud and software', 'Hardware' and 'Services' expense lines; those three are combined here as cost of revenue. Net income of $3,721M is before $22M of preferred stock dividends; the $1.27 EPS uses the $3,699M available to common shareholders.
